rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: HARM: the rule exists so bold keeps its scan value on a projected slide — when a whole sentence or a whole title is bolded, bold stops marking a handle and starts decorating prose, and a reader loses the ability to find the actual named terms at a glance. That harm is present in both loci below, not merely the rule's shape matching. (a) Chunk 2 'Prework' line 10: `**A real slice you'd send off rather than nudge bit by bit. Bigger than a typo-fix, smaller than an epic.**` bolds a full ~20-word narrative statement — no coined term/law/checklist name here — matching the banned shape verbatim ('never a whole lead sentence'; 'Narrative...prose = no bold'). (b) Chunk 8 'Pre-reads before Module 5' (a reading-list/menu slide, confirmed by its own header matching the compendium's own example 'pre-reads, a menu of options'): lines 69, 71, 73, 75 each bold the ENTIRE mode+title span, e.g. line 69 `**Read, [Clean Code Is Steering: Reading Uncle Bob's Agent Experiments](...).** ` and line 75 `**Read (longer), Kieran Klaassen, [Compound Engineering: The Definitive Guide](...).** `. The per-slide ≤1 budget is correctly off here (menu carve-out applies), but the ≲5-word handle cap is explicitly NOT off, and the rule names this exact shape by name: 'Bolding mode-plus-title is the pre-2026-07-09 monoculture wearing a list for cover.' All four entries bold past 5 words and include the full title/author/link text, contrary to 'bold the mode word alone (`**Read:**`, `**Watch:**`) and leave the title plain.' Checked the maintainer block (lines 81-167) for an existing accept-note on either passage — none found. `grep -n "\*\*.*\*\*"` against lines 1-80 confirms both loci at the cited line numbers.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Line 10: unbold to plain prose, or trim to a short handle if one exists. Lines 69/71/73/75: bold only the mode word (`**Read,**` / `**Watch,**`), leave the bracketed title, author, and link plain.
